non_scope: The AI Agent Runtime (NXS-P13): prompt orchestration, model-provider selection, an autonomous planning loop, and vendor-specific tool_call parsing
Workflow / DAG orchestration, scheduling and campaigns (NXS-P14 / NXS-P15 / NXS-P16)
HTTP / OpenAPI / GraphQL / CRM / ERP / calendar execution itself — that stays owned by the NXS-P07 Integration Hub; the Tool Engine only orchestrates invocation through it
A production external secret vault — P07 owns the vault seam; the Tool Engine never handles secret material
Channel providers: WhatsApp / email / SMS / telephony / ElevenLabs (NXS-P09+)
Metering, cost and billing of tool calls (NXS-P23)
The full observability / audit platform (NXS-P22 / NXS-P24) — P08 emits structured logs, execution receipts and P04 events only
Human-in-the-loop approval UI and autonomous approval behaviour
A generic arbitrary-execution endpoint of any kind (run-anything, raw shell, arbitrary Python / SQL / URL proxy / GraphQL executor)
objective: Build the permanent Nexus AI Tool Engine boundary that governs how an LLM / caller invokes actions: a tenant-owned Tool Registry of deterministic, versioned ToolDefinitions (stable tool_key + organization scope + version + input/output JSON Schema + required permissions + risk class + side-effect classification + idempotency policy + timeout policy + optional integration binding to an NXS-P07 integration_id + operation_key + enabled state), a deterministic tool-invocation policy pipeline (tenant context -> tool existence -> enabled state -> version resolution -> caller principal -> server-side RBAC / permission requirement -> organization/tool policy -> argument schema validation -> side-effect / risk policy -> durable idempotency / replay rules -> integration binding -> governed NXS-P07 execution -> normalized result validation -> execution receipt + P04 event), a normalized ToolResult with a stable RFC 9457 / NXS_TOOL_* error taxonomy, and durable execution idempotency scoped by organization / tool / idempotency_key with request fingerprinting (same key + same fingerprint may replay the stored result; same key + different fingerprint fails deterministically; exactly-once is NOT claimed). The Tool Engine NEVER bypasses the Integration Hub: every external call routes through NXS-INT-001, and the LLM / caller never receives a plaintext secret, a raw credential, an unrestricted URL / method / header set, an arbitrary GraphQL document, a direct database handle or a provider SDK credential. A model / caller chooses only a registered tool by stable identifier plus validated arguments; there is no generic arbitrary-execution endpoint (no /tool/run-anything, no /http/request, no raw shell / Python / SQL / URL proxy / GraphQL executor). Default deny: an unregistered, unauthorized, disabled or schema-invalid invocation, and one missing the required integration permission, is rejected. Tenant isolation is a PostgreSQL boundary (organization_id canonical, forced RLS, tenant-aware FKs, no cross-tenant adoption; reversible migrations). Proven by unit, integration, security (arbitrary / unregistered tool, cross-tenant lookup + invoke, permission bypass, disabled tool, forged organization_id, schema bypass, extra arguments, key confusion, secret exfiltration, raw credential exposure, URL / method / header / GraphQL injection, operation_key tampering, idempotency key reuse with a different payload, result poisoning, fail-open config), concurrency (same-key convergence, registration / version conflict) and resilience (timeout, downstream Integration Hub error mapping, circuit / rate-limit propagation, retries never duplicating unsafe side effects, transaction rollback integrity) test matrices, reversible migrations with forced RLS and tenant-aware FKs, multi-architecture builds and a clean-room validation on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
title: Tool Engine
